resources.string: Codex limits on your ChatGPT plan
Usage limits of your Claude plan
AIMeter shows how much is left on your ChatGPT (Codex) and Claude plans. Everything stays on this phone.
All your accounts are hidden from Home. You can show them again in Accounts.
The session expired. Reconnect the account to keep seeing its usage.
No figures yet. Pull down to refresh.
Order your accounts and choose which ones show on Home and in the notification. Hidden accounts keep refreshing.
Open the Codex verification page in your browser, copy the device code, and finish authorization there.
Use %1$s device-code login. The authorization code is shown here and can also be copied from the login notification.
Generate a device code, then enter it in the Codex verification page.
Tap Open verification page to continue in your browser. AIMeter is polling for authorization.
Authorization received. Exchanging it for a Codex session…
Validating the session with Codex quota usage…
Authorization completed, but quota validation failed. You can retry validation without generating a new code.
The authorized account does not match the expected account.
This is not the account you were re-authenticating. Add it as a new account instead?
This authorization code expired. Generate a new one to continue.
Codex sign-in failed. Generate a new code to retry.
Add an account to show quota in the app, widget, and notification.
This deletes the session and local history of %1$s from this device.
Notification, refresh, alerts, data, and diagnostics preferences.
This applies to the app. Home-screen widgets always follow the system light/dark theme.
A low-noise quota status in the notification shade.
Android is blocking this app\'s notifications. Turn the switch on to allow them.
Choose which account the persistent notification displays.
Choose the quota window shown in the persistent notification.
Notify on tight and exhausted states for the primary quota window.
Notify when an account needs to sign in again or several refreshes in a row fail.
Used only for the optional status, quota alerts, and account-error alerts. The app and widget work without it.
Tight and exhausted primary quota alerts.
Connect an account to show quota status.
Primary quota remaining is near the tight threshold.
Primary quota has reached the limit.
Log in again to keep quota refresh working.
Recent refresh failed. Last known quota remains visible.
Open the %1$s verification page, then use Copy code to paste the authorization code.
Return to AIMeter to generate a new authorization code.
Return to AIMeter to retry. Safe reason: %1$s.
Authorization finished, but quota validation did not pass. Safe reason: %1$s.
Tap to connect an AI provider
Choose the account and which quota fields to show. The widget shows the first 1–4 fields based on its size.
No saved account yet. Add an account in AIMeter first.
Show up to %1$d fields (by widget size)
Show every account visible on Home, or only the ones you choose.
Refresh all accounts in the background when Android allows it.
Battery saving delays refresh while the screen is off. In the battery settings, turn off optimization for AIMeter to keep refresh closer to your interval.
How often to refresh quota in the background.
Local quota history is kept for trends and diagnostics only.
Removes all quota history; keeps accounts and sessions.
This clears local quota history for all accounts. Accounts and encrypted sessions stay on this device.
Diagnostics are collapsed until copied or refreshed.
Usage data comes from each provider\'s own servers. These usage endpoints are not publicly documented and may change.

Sign-in tokens are stored on this device, encrypted with an Android Keystore key. The app only talks to the providers\' own servers (OpenAI for Codex, Anthropic for Claude). There is no developer server, analytics, ads or telemetry.

AIMeter is an independent app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by OpenAI or Anthropic. Codex, ChatGPT and Claude are trademarks of their owners; they only name the services whose limits the app shows.
The session expired or was revoked. Sign in to this account again.

The provider is temporarily limiting requests. The app will try again later.
The provider\'s server did not respond correctly. The app will try again later.
The provider\'s answer could not be read as usage data.
Sign-in happens on claude.ai in your browser. This app never sees your password or your browser cookies; it only receives a one-time authorization code on this device.
The authorization page will name Claude Code: Anthropic offers no public sign-in for other apps, so this app uses the public sign-in client of Anthropic\'s Claude Code CLI.

Permission requested: user:profile. The app uses it only to read your profile and usage limits. It does not request user:inference (sending messages with your plan) or org:create_api_key (creating API keys). Anthropic does not document everything user:profile allows, so do not treat the token as read-only: it is a credential for your Claude account.
The tokens stay on this device, encrypted with an Android Keystore key. Disconnecting deletes them from the device; Anthropic provides no way for this app to revoke the authorization on its servers.

Anthropic\'s terms reserve this sign-in for Claude Code and Anthropic\'s own apps, and Anthropic may restrict accounts that use it elsewhere. Continue only if you accept that risk. Without signing in, you can check usage in the official Claude app or on claude.ai under Settings > Usage.
Finish signing in with the browser. When the page says you are signed in, close it to return here.
You can close this tab and return to the app.
Close this tab and try again from AIMeter.
No browser is available to open the Claude sign-in page.
Could not open the local return channel for the sign-in on this device. Try again.
The sign-in was cancelled or denied in the browser.
Claude did not accept the requested permission (user:profile).
Claude returned an error instead of a sign-in code. Try again.
The sign-in took too long and was stopped. Try again.
Claude rejected the sign-in code. Start the sign-in again.
Claude accepted the sign-in but refused to report usage for it. Nothing was saved.
You signed in to a different Claude account. The existing account was not changed.
The app deletes the sign-in tokens, usage history and widget data of %1$s from this device and asks OpenAI to revoke the sign-in. If the revocation fails, the local data is deleted anyway.

The app deletes the sign-in tokens, usage history and widget data of %1$s from this device. Anthropic offers no way for apps to revoke this sign-in remotely. Your browser\'s claude.ai session is not affected.

Sign-in happens on auth.openai.com, in the browser, the same way as codex login. This app never sees the password or the browser\'s cookies; it only receives, on this device, a one-time authorization code.

OpenAI does not offer a sign-in for other apps, so this one uses the public sign-in client of Codex CLI, OpenAI\'s command-line tool. It does not need the device-code option in ChatGPT\'s security settings.

Requested permissions: openid, profile, email and offline_access (account identity and renewing access); Codex CLI also asks for connector permissions this app does not use. The token belongs to your ChatGPT account and is not read-only; the app only uses it to read Codex usage.
Tokens stay on this device, encrypted with an Android Keystore key. Disconnecting asks OpenAI to revoke the access and deletes them from the device.
No browser is available to open the OpenAI sign-in page.
The sign-in\'s local return channel could not be opened (ports 1455 and 1457 are in use on this device). Close the app using them and try again.
OpenAI returned an error instead of a sign-in code. Try again.
This ChatGPT account has no access to Codex.
OpenAI refused the sign-in code. Start again.
OpenAI accepted the sign-in but refused to report Codex usage. Nothing was saved.
You signed in to another ChatGPT account. The existing account was not changed.
Only works after enabling device-code sign-in in ChatGPT\'s security settings (on the web).
%1$s: the data on this device was deleted and the provider accepted the request to revoke the sign-in.
%1$s: the data on this device was deleted. The provider offers no remote revocation for this sign-in.
%1$s: the data on this device was deleted, but the provider did not confirm the revocation (no connection or an error answer). On the provider\'s side the sign-in may stay valid until it expires.
Open the app and sign in to this account again.
No usage data yet. Tap refresh or open the app.
The provider reported no limits to show.
